question: When can a changed measurement standard count as local progress when its readings change meaning?
scope: Only standards fully assessed on one fixed, independently justified, task-specific obligation set; no claim of global scientific progress.

definitions.task_profile: A versioned, precomparison record of task uses, tested cases, warranted obligations, reasons and evidence rules.
definitions.obligation_set: Finite set O_T of independently justified distinctions or outcomes to be assessed under profile T.
definitions.met_set: G_T(S), the obligations in O_T met by standard S on the shared evidence.
definitions.improvement: S ≺_T S2 iff G_T(S) is a strict subset of G_T(S2), both complete on the same O_T.

premises.claim: A progress claim needs an explicit basis of comparison.
A single score may hide task-relevant distinctions or impose unjustified exchange rates.
premises.role: conceptual; needs literature and case examination

premises.claim: A fixed task can warrant several obligations separately without ordering all trade-offs.
premises.role: central substantive premise; task justification is contestable

premises.claim: Set inclusion preserves all earlier met obligations and identifies additional met obligations without summing them.
Strict set inclusion is transitive and asymmetric on a fixed obligation universe.

steps: Fix T, its obligation universe, case set and evidence rules before seeing comparative outputs.
Evaluate each standard against every obligation using common evidence; unknown outcomes block a complete comparison.
Compare met sets by strict inclusion; do not weight or total the obligations.
Infer only a local, conditional improvement claim; conflicting outcomes yield incomparability.
inference.conclusion: A standard may improve locally across representational change without a scalar total accuracy measure, if it preserves prior warranted success and adds success on the same fixed profile.

obligations.O1: choose lower-miss system for the predeclared high-miss-cost use; scalar tie A/B cannot resolve, vector can select A
obligations.O2: choose lower-false-alarm system for the predeclared nuisance-cost use; scalar tie A/B cannot resolve, vector can select B
obligations.O3: preserve C ahead of D, which is better in both dimensions; scalar and vector both do so

result.relation: strict inclusion, conditional on the stipulated task rationale and correct assessment

limits: No empirical detector or user behavior is asserted.
The task profile and evidence must be fixed before testing.
Actual robustness and practical costs are untested.

objections.source: Astra assessor, separately attributed critical challenge; session 01a0dbb8-f987-7ab3-887f-5f4d38ed758a
objections.challenge: Can the relation avoid cycles without reinstating the complete master ordering it rejects?
objections.response: Strict set inclusion on the same T is acyclic by transitivity and asymmetry; it reinstates neither a scalar nor a total ordering. The result fails to cover task switching, which must be marked incomparable without a justified bridge.

objections.source: Sol assessor assessment; no separate contribution ID declared
objections.challenge: The task-relative comparison may be cyclic and may select a task that encodes the desired verdict.
objections.response: Freeze task obligations before candidate outputs, document independent reasons, use candidate-blind specification and sensitivity/held-out checks. These controls reduce but cannot eliminate normative contestability; if no stable justified profile remains, withdraw the comparison.

objections.source: Root selection reason as substantive AI orchestration
objections.challenge: Preserve distinctions without silently substituting another scalar master measure; prevent task switching and cycles.
objections.response: Use an unweighted obligation set and allow incomparability. Narrow the claim to one fixed task profile; do not infer global progress across differing profiles.

falsifiers_or_narrowing_conditions: Candidate-blind, independently justified task profiles do not support the key obligations.
The apparent gain requires a post hoc threshold, dropped obligation, or hidden weighting.
A real replacement loses a previously met obligation, so strict inclusion fails.
No cross-version obligations can be defended because concepts/cases shift too far.
Relevant primary literature already supplies the same criterion, requiring a new contribution or abandonment.
